title: Sandy Beaches in Vis, Croatia: What Is Real in 2027
metaDescription: Vis has no large sandy beach. Here are the sand and fine-pebble spots (Milna, Zaglav, Stončica, Grandovac) and the nearest true sand, with access tips.
content:
## Does Vis Have Sandy Beaches?

No. Vis has no long, true sandy beach of the kind found in Nin or on parts of Mljet. What exists are a few small coves where sand mixes with fine pebble. Everything else is pebble, rock slab or concrete bathing platform. The closest reliable sand is Bačvice in Split, reached by the Vis–Split ferry or catamaran, which takes from about 1 hour 10 minutes (fast catamaran) to about 2 hours 20 minutes (car ferry).

## Beach Surfaces on Vis at a Glance

The island is limestone. Most coves are made of rounded pebbles, flat rock or both. Sand only appears in sheltered bays on the east and southeast side, where it collects in small amounts. Expect sand underfoot only in the first few metres of water. Pebbles often start beyond that.

## The Best Sand and Fine-Pebble Beaches on Vis

### Milna

Milna is the island's best bet for sand. It is a small bay on the southeast coast facing a group of islets. The surface is sand mixed with fine pebble, and the water stays knee-deep for a long way out. That makes it the most useful beach on Vis for toddlers and young children. Shade is limited, so bring an umbrella. Parking is informal and fills up by late morning in July and August. A car or scooter is needed, because there is no regular bus here.

### Zaglav

Zaglav sits close to Milna and has a similar surface of sand and fine pebble. The entry is gentle and the water is calm. It is smaller than Milna and has fewer parking spaces. Together the two beaches make a practical pair for one morning. Visit Zaglav first if Milna looks crowded.

### Stončica

Stončica is on the northeast coast near Vis town and has a small bay with fine pebble and sandy patches. The pine trees give natural shade. The water is shallow near the shore and calm, which works for children. It is small, so it fills up on summer weekends. Reach it by car, scooter or bicycle from Vis town in under 15 minutes. Parking is limited.

### Grandovac

Grandovac, in Kut at the eastern edge of Vis town, is a family beach with fine pebble and concrete platforms. Some listings call it sandy, but pebble is what you will actually stand on. The entry is gradual and the water is calm. It is crowded in peak season, since it is the closest beach to town. Walking from the harbour takes about 25 to 30 minutes along the waterfront, and that is easier than looking for parking.

## Pebble Beaches Often Mistaken for Sand

### Srebrna

Srebrna is a pebble and stone-slab beach on the south coast. Its pine trees provide good shade. A parking area sits about 250 m from the beach. Children can use it, but the pebbles are larger than at Milna, so water shoes help. It is popular, so arrive before 10:00 in July and August.

### Stiniva

Stiniva is a pebble cove between two cliffs. It is reached on foot by a steep path of roughly 20 minutes, or by boat. It has no sand, almost no shade and a steep path that is a poor choice for small children. Treat it as a photo stop, not a sand beach.

### Prirovo and Komiža

Prirovo, the town beach in Vis, is pebble and concrete. The beaches of Komiža, including Gusarica, are pebble. Some online lists label them sandy, but they are not.

## Nearest Real Sandy Beaches Outside Vis

Bačvice in Split is the practical choice. It has sand, shallow water, showers, shops and good transport links. It is a city beach, so it is busy. Plan it as a day on the mainland around ferry times. The Vis–Split ferry is the only regular link, so check the timetable before you plan a return the same day. Other large sandy areas around Nin and Zadar are much further away, so they are not a realistic detour from Vis.

## Insider Tips

- Go to Milna and Zaglav in the morning, since the wind and the crowd are lighter before midday.
- Pack water shoes for every Vis beach, including the sandy ones, because the pebbles begin quickly.
- Bring your own shade at Milna, Zaglav and Grandovac.
- Rent a scooter or car. Public transport to the south and southeast coast is limited.
- Do not remove pebbles from Srebrna. It is prohibited.

## Verdict: Is Vis Good for People Who Want Sand?

Only in small doses. Milna and Zaglav deliver sand and very shallow water, and they are a good fit for families with small children. The reality is that these are small coves with limited parking and little shade, so a week of sandcastle holidays here will disappoint. Do not choose Vis for sand. Choose it for clear water and quiet pebble coves, and add Milna or Zaglav as a sand fix. If sand is the priority, go to the mainland instead.

faq.question: Does Vis have a sandy beach?
faq.answer: Not a true one. Vis has small coves with sand mixed with fine pebble, mainly Milna, Zaglav and Stončica. Most other beaches are pebble or rock.

faq.question: Which beach on Vis is best for small children?
faq.answer: Milna is the best choice because the water stays very shallow and the surface is sand and fine pebble. Zaglav is similar. Grandovac is also suitable for families and is easier to reach from Vis town.

faq.question: Is Stiniva a sandy beach?
faq.answer: No. Stiniva is a pebble cove between two cliffs. It is reached by a steep path of roughly 20 minutes or by boat, and offers little shade.

faq.question: Where is the nearest real sandy beach to Vis?
faq.answer: Bačvice in Split is the most practical, with sand and shallow water. The fast catamaran from Vis takes about 1 hour 10 minutes, and the car ferry about 2 hours 20 minutes.

faq.question: Do I need a car to reach the sandy beaches on Vis?
faq.answer: A car or scooter is the easiest way, especially for Milna and Zaglav. Grandovac is within walking distance of Vis town, and Stončica is reachable by bicycle.

quickAnswer: Vis has no true sandy beach. The best options are small mixed sand and fine-pebble coves: Milna, Zaglav and Stončica. Grandovac is fine pebble and concrete, and Srebrna and Stiniva are pebble. The nearest real sand is Bačvice in Split, about 1 hour 10 minutes to 2 hours 20 minutes away by boat.
